title: TERRESTRIAL WORLD GLOBE CIRCA ...
description: TERRESTRIAL WORLD GLOBE CIRCA 1970'S - AS IS
findings: Illuminated terrestrial desk globe on a clear acrylic cradle and round foot, with an electric flex and old dark plug at the back. A booklet in front reads 'NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC Globe' with 'A guide to its use and ... place names' on a space-themed cover (a line ending 'Cartographer', name not legible). So this is probably a National Geographic Society globe, which the title does not say. No maker name, copyright date or edition is legible on the globe itself. Map is the shaded-relief political style with Australia in peach and ocean names in spaced italic lettering. Web check (19/10/2026): a library catalogue record at https://oshermaps.org/browse-maps?id=114992 shows the same booklet title for a 1961 edition. The date of this copy is not legible, so the title's 'circa 1970s' is neither confirmed nor contradicted.
condition: Acrylic cradle yellowed and cloudy with scuffs. Map faded with light surface wear. Old flex and plug, working order unknown (sold as is).
reason: Probably a National Geographic illuminated globe with its booklet, maker not named in the title; modest upside.
marks_read: Booklet cover: NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC Globe, 'A guide to its use and ... place names' (partly legible). Globe itself: no maker or date legible.

title: BAKELITE & CHROME STANDARD LAM...
description: BAKELITE & CHROME STANDARD LAMP CIRCA 1955 H-168 CM
findings: Art Deco style floor lamp: slim chrome tube stem with a black sleeve or telescopic joint part way down, a black fluted tapering column (looks like Bakelite or ebonised timber, consistent with the title) with two chrome collars, a polished chrome cup at the foot and a round black base with a beaded metal rim. The bell shaped peach silk shade looks like a later replacement. No maker's mark, label or patent number visible (lamp holder and underside not photographed). The form matches the chrome and Bakelite floor lamps of the 1930s: a web search (19/10/2026) found Carters, an Australian auction house, with sold lots of similar Art Deco chrome and Bakelite floor lamps (166 and 172 cm, round bases with bead trim; the 172 cm one described as circa 1930s with fluted details to the lower part). Prices were not seen and I could not open those pages, for example https://carters.com.au/index.cfm/item/1225374-an-art-deco-chrome-and-black-bakelite-floor-lamp-circa-1930s-a-s . So the title's 'circa 1955' may be too late, but the age cannot be confirmed from the photos. Height of 168 cm in the title is not checkable.
condition: Chrome looks dulled or tarnished in places and the base rim shows wear. Black parts look intact in the photos. Flex and plug look old and would need an electrical check. Shade is probably not original.
reason: Classic Art Deco chrome and Bakelite standard lamp, a type collectors and decorators chase when sound and rewired; no marks to add value.

title: JANZEN SUNSHINE SUPERMAN ORIGI...
findings: Large flat-colour advertising poster printed 'jantzen SUNSHINE SUPERMAN'. The catalogue title spells the maker 'Janzen', so a search for Jantzen may miss it. Three muscled men in 1960s to 70s swimwear (striped knit top, floral trunks, red and white striped shorts) in front of a pink, yellow and orange sunburst on a red ground with a green border, heavy black outlines. No printer's imprint, date or signature is legible in the photo. The only small mark is a short black L-shaped stroke on the right hand figure's leg, which looks like part of the drawing. Photographed held by binder clips at top and bottom, not framed or backed. Web check (pages read 19/10/2026): the same dealer copy, item CL197-101, 'Jantzen Sunshine Superman', c1970s colour screenprint, 99.8 x 66.7 cm, 'Repaired minor tears and missing portions to edges. Linen-backed.', is shown at AUD $1,250 at https://www.joseflebovicgallery.com/pages/books/CL197-101/jantzen-sunshine-superman and at AUD $1,000, marked 'Sold out', at https://www.postersandprints.com.au/products/jantzen-sunshine-superman . These are dealer asking prices for one repaired copy, not realised auction prices. The Armitage poster's proportions match that size, but its size, age and originality cannot be proven from the photo.
condition: Colours bright and the green border looks complete on all sides. Top edge ripples and curls between the two binder clips. No tears, folds or stains visible at photo size, but the clip areas and the back are hidden. Size not stated in the title.
reason: Jantzen Sunshine Superman c1970s advertising poster, a listed collectable catalogued under a misspelt maker name; a specialist dealer asks four figures for a repaired copy (see findings).
marks_read: Printed title 'jantzen SUNSHINE SUPERMAN'; no printer imprint, date or signature legible; small black L-shaped stroke on right figure's leg (looks like drawing detail)
